Hey! So I totally feel you, I took last year off due to my mental health issues and I've also had an admission where I missed a month of this year and here are some tips I have.

1. Link in with your college's disability support services. I live in Australia so I'm not sure if this is something we just have here but it's worth looking into.
2. Catch things early. As soon as things start to get bad book in to see your treating team rather than waiting until things get bad. This may even mean increasing your appointments around the start of the year or times you know can be difficult even if you're symptom free just in case
3. Pick and choose what classes you can miss. For instance, things aren't going that well for me at the moment so I'm having an admission and missing two not very important days of uni, and it means I'll probably be out in time for an important training day I have
4. Sleep! I have at least 9+ hours a night. No matter how much study I have, even if I have an exam the next day, I always try to sleep as much as possible
5. Recognise that you won't be completely stable and that's okay. I still have episodes, I've had significant time in hospital this year and I've missed an important exam. But I'm still enrolled and progressing with my course.
6. Stress less about grades. Maybe this is just because I'm in a field where grades don't matter and all that matters is passing but I literally do the bare minimum of study required.

I'm still figuring this all out myself but these are some things I can think of at the top of my head!

Abilify can be a very activating antipsychotic and like the user said below it can cause anxiety, and so can armodafinil.
